new_candidates.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Callers that need both the spatial velocity Jacobian and its Hessian call `CalcJacobianSpatialVelocity()` and then `CalcHessianSpatialVelocity()` with the same arguments. One example is `ManipulabilityCost` (#25234). Internally, the Hessian already computes the world Jacobians of B and A at P, so every gradient evaluation builds J twice. On an iiwa with a warm cache, the caller's own J call costs about 280 ns, next to about 720 ns for the Hessian itself.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
An optional output parameter on `CalcHessianSpatialVelocity()`, e.g. `EigenPtr<MatrixX<T>> Js_V_ABp_E = nullptr`. It would be filled with exactly what `CalcJacobianSpatialVelocity()` returns for the same `with_respect_to`, `frame_B`, `p_BP`, `frame_A` and `frame_E`. The function already holds `Js_V_WBp` and `Js_V_WAp`, so this costs one subtraction and one re-expression in E.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- A separate `CalcJacobianAndHessianSpatialVelocity()` function. It adds API surface for the same result.
- Caching J in the `Context`. MbP can't declare per-frame-pair cache entries after `Finalize()`.

Self-assigning, and just opening the issue to hear feedback on the interface before I implement a fix. cc @sherm1 @SeanCurtis-TRI -- I would love to hear your thoughts!
new_candidates.title: MultibodyPlant::CalcHessianSpatialVelocity: optionally return the Jacobian it computes

In Drake we have rules to install third-party licenses, like this:

https://github.com/RobotLocomotion/drake/blob/9a17a045ff1144e97615e2fba9ce55bb75408f1b/tools/workspace/eigen/BUILD.bazel#L83-L92

That style of `rules_license` declarations is mothballed, with the new hotness being `@package_metadata`.

Example of old:
- https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel-central-registry/blob/main/modules/fmt/11.2.0.bcr.2/overlay/BUILD.bazel#L18

Example of new:
- https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel-central-registry/blob/main/modules/fmt/12.2.1/overlay/BUILD.bazel#L31

Modules in BCR are moving to use `package_metadata` now.  I'm generally trying to convince them to keep _both_ annotations around for a transition period, but I'm not always successful.

We should start porting our `//:install` ruleset to allow pointing at `package_metadata` information instead of `rules_license`, and switch to using that for BCR modules that offer it.

The main chunk of work will be doing the first port, with associated starlark installer infra changes in Drake.  After that, adding more should hopefully be easy.

This should be a non-functional change -- the list of installed files (and where they end up) in a tar.gz release artifact should not change.

new_candidates.body:
In pydrake, a `LeafSystem` that stores the result of `DeclareCacheEntry()` on itself is never garbage collected.

## Reproduction

```python
import gc
import weakref

from pydrake.common.value import Value
from pydrake.systems.framework import LeafSystem, ValueProducer


class MySystem(LeafSystem):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.entry = self.DeclareCacheEntry(
            description="entry",
            value_producer=ValueProducer(
                allocate=lambda: Value[object](None),
                calc=lambda context, value: None,
            ),
        )


system = MySystem()
ref = weakref.ref(system)
del system
for _ in range(3):
    gc.collect()
print("freed:", ref() is None)  # Expected True.
```

Actual: `freed: False`, with both pybind11 and nanobind (Python 3.12.3). If the line stores nothing (`self.DeclareCacheEntry(...)` with the result discarded), the system is freed. The same happens when the entry comes from `self.get_cache_entry(index)` instead.

## Cause

`SystemBase.DeclareCacheEntry` and `get_cache_entry` return the entry with `py_rvp::reference_internal`, which adds a `keep_alive` from the returned entry to the system. Python's garbage collector can't see `keep_alive`. Storing the entry on the system adds a visible edge in the other direction, so the pair forms a cycle that the collector can never break.

The port getters in the same file already avoid this. They use `py_rvp::reference` with `ref_cycle<0, 1>`, and a comment says why ("rather than the implicit keep-alive of reference_internal").

## Affected

- `bindings/pydrake/systems/framework_py_systems.cc`: `DeclareCacheEntry` and `get_cache_entry`.
- `bindings/pydrake/multibody/tree_py.cc`: `ForceDensityField.DeclareCacheEntry` returns with `py_rvp::reference` plus `keep_alive<0, 1>`. It has the same shape, but I haven't probed it separately.

## Why tests don't catch it

`memory_leak_test.py` declares a cache entry but never stores the returned entry, so only the producer callbacks are checked.

## Possible fix

Return the entry with `py_rvp::reference` and `ref_cycle<0, 1>`, like the port getters. That requires the `CacheEntry` class to be tracked by the garbage collector (`py::dynamic_attr()`), which I haven't checked. Add a case to `memory_leak_test.py` that stores the entry on the system.

## Related

Found while working on the issue "investigate uses of WrapCallbacks() for memory leaks". This is a different mechanism from the callback holds fixed there: a hidden `keep_alive` edge that closes a cycle the user creates, not a C++ `shared_ptr` that holds a callable. A `MakeWitnessFunction` result stored on the system, and `Diagram` and `DiagramBuilder` subsystem getters, did not leak when I probed them.
new_candidates.title: [pydrake] Storing the result of DeclareCacheEntry on a LeafSystem leaks the system

new_candidates.body:
### Describe the bug

We reset our scene a lot (stop, respawn objects, play), and after a few dozen resets in the same process objects start rendering in the wrong place. A bowl disappears, and later a gripper part shows up inside it. Nothing is logged.

It seems to come down to cameras. Every reset re-initializes each `Camera`, and each time Isaac Lab tags the camera prims with Fabric attributes under brand-new names (`isaaclab:fabricXform:<uid>:*` in `FabricXformSelection` and `isaaclab:cameraIntrinsicRow:<uuid>` in the RTX renderer). The old ones get removed, but the names keep growing, and after roughly a thousand of them Fabric quietly stops updating newly created prims. The Fabric side is reported in isaac-sim/IsaacSim#943.

More cameras make it happen sooner: about 24 resets with 8 cameras, 48 with 4, 97 with 2.

### Steps to reproduce

The script below spawns a cube and a few cameras, then loops stop / respawn / reset / step and checks the cube's Fabric transforms. No assets needed.

```
./isaaclab.sh -p repro_camera_reinit.py --num_cameras 8
...
cycle 23: ok
cycle 24: BROKEN ['/World/Objects/Cuboid world=[0.   0.2  0.09] expected=[0. 0. 0.]']
```

<details><summary>repro_camera_reinit.py</summary>

```python
"""Camera re-initialization breaks Fabric world matrices after ~1000 new attribute sets (Isaac Lab 3.0.0, PhysX).

Each cycle stops the sim, respawns one rigid cuboid, resets and steps. Every reset re-initializes every Camera, and
each re-initialization authors freshly named Fabric attributes (isaaclab:fabricXform:{uid}:* and
isaaclab:cameraIntrinsicRow:{uuid}). After roughly 1000 new attribute sets the Fabric hierarchy stops keeping
omni:fabric:worldMatrix == omni:fabric:localMatrix x parent worldMatrix for newly created prims, and RTX draws them
in the wrong place. With 4 cameras this happens at cycle ~48, with 8 at ~24, with 2 at ~97.

    ./isaaclab.sh -p repro_camera_reinit.py --num_cameras 4
"""

import argparse

from isaaclab.app import AppLauncher

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument("--num_cameras", type=int, default=4)
parser.add_argument("--cycles", type=int, default=100)
AppLauncher.add_app_launcher_args(parser)
args = parser.parse_args()
args.headless = True
args.enable_cameras = True
app = AppLauncher(args).app

import numpy as np  # noqa: E402
import omni.usd  # noqa: E402
import usdrt  # noqa: E402
from pxr import Usd  # noqa: E402

import isaaclab.sim as sim_utils  # noqa: E402
from isaaclab.assets import RigidObject, RigidObjectCfg  # noqa: E402
from isaaclab.sensors import Camera, CameraCfg  # noqa: E402

ROOT = "/World/Objects"

sim = sim_utils.SimulationContext(sim_utils.SimulationCfg(dt=0.01))
sim_utils.GroundPlaneCfg().func("/World/ground", sim_utils.GroundPlaneCfg())
sim_utils.DistantLightCfg(intensity=3000.0).func("/World/light", sim_utils.DistantLightCfg(intensity=3000.0))
sim_utils.create_prim(ROOT, "Xform")
cameras = [
    Camera(
        CameraCfg(
            prim_path=f"/World/camera_{i}",
            height=180,
            width=320,
            data_types=["rgb"],
            spawn=sim_utils.PinholeCameraCfg(),
            offset=CameraCfg.OffsetCfg(pos=(1.5, 0.1 * i, 1.0), rot=(0.0, 0.2588, 0.0, 0.9659), convention="world"),
        )
    )
    for i in range(args.num_cameras)
]


def spawn_cuboid(cycle: int) -> RigidObject:
    return RigidObject(
        RigidObjectCfg(
            prim_path=f"{ROOT}/Cuboid",
            spawn=sim_utils.CuboidCfg(
                size=(0.1, 0.1, 0.1),
                rigid_props=sim_utils.RigidBodyPropertiesCfg(),
                mass_props=sim_utils.MassPropertiesCfg(mass=0.2),
                collision_props=sim_utils.CollisionPropertiesCfg(),
            ),
            init_state=RigidObjectCfg.InitialStateCfg(pos=(0.0, 0.05 * (cycle % 5), 0.1)),
        )
    )


def matrix(prim: usdrt.Usd.Prim, name: str) -> np.ndarray | None:
    attr = prim.GetAttribute(name) if prim else None
    return np.array(attr.Get(), dtype=float).reshape(4, 4) if attr and attr.HasValue() else None


def inconsistent_prims() -> list[str]:
    """Prims under ROOT whose Fabric world matrix is not local x parent world."""
    fabric = usdrt.Usd.Stage.Attach(omni.usd.get_context().get_stage_id())
    root = omni.usd.get_context().get_stage().GetPrimAtPath(ROOT)
    bad = []
    for usd_prim in Usd.PrimRange(root):
        if usd_prim == root:
            continue
        prim = fabric.GetPrimAtPath(str(usd_prim.GetPath()))
        world = matrix(prim, "omni:fabric:worldMatrix")
        local = matrix(prim, "omni:fabric:localMatrix")
        parent = matrix(fabric.GetPrimAtPath(str(usd_prim.GetParent().GetPath())), "omni:fabric:worldMatrix")
        if world is not None and local is not None and parent is not None:
            expected = local @ parent
            if np.abs(expected[3, :3] - world[3, :3]).max() > 0.01:
                bad.append(f"{usd_prim.GetPath()} world={world[3, :3].round(2)} expected={expected[3, :3].round(2)}")
    return bad


cuboid = None
for cycle in range(1, args.cycles + 1):
    if sim.is_playing():
        sim.stop()
    if cuboid is not None:
        sim_utils.delete_prim(f"{ROOT}/Cuboid")
    cuboid = spawn_cuboid(cycle)
    sim.reset()
    for _ in range(2):
        sim.step(render=True)
        for camera in cameras:
            camera.update(sim.get_physics_dt())
    bad = inconsistent_prims()
    print(f"cycle {cycle}: {'BROKEN ' + str(bad) if bad else 'ok'}", flush=True)
    if bad:
        break
app.close()
```

</details>

### Possible fix

Reuse a name once its attributes have been removed from every prim, instead of always taking a new one. That keeps the existing guarantee that a dead view's leftovers never match a live one. With this patch the repro stays clean (120+ cycles with 8 cameras), our own setup went from breaking at reset 41 to 150+ clean resets, and the Fabric view and RTX renderer tests still pass. It applies to v3.0.0, `release/3.0.0` and `main`. Happy to open a PR.

new_candidates.body:
### Description

After a process has created about 1000 distinct Fabric attribute sets (buckets), prims created afterwards no longer satisfy `omni:fabric:worldMatrix == omni:fabric:localMatrix x parent worldMatrix`. 

Objects vanish or render at another prim's pose. Nothing is logged, and `IFabricHierarchy.update_world_xforms()` and `Rt.Xformable.SetWorldXformFromUsd()` don't repair anything.

The bug can be reproduced like that:

- Each cycle: create K uniquely named `UInt` attributes via `usdrt` `CreateAttribute`, render, `RemoveProperty` them; delete and respawn a PhysX rigid cuboid; stop/reset/step with one RTX camera.
- K attributes on K different prims: breaks at cycle 108 / 85 / 48 / 27 for K = 4 / 8 / 16 / 32 (about 1000 new sets in total).
- The same K attributes on a single prim (more intermediate attribute sets): breaks sooner, cycle 59 for K = 8.
- Reusing the same K names every cycle: no break within 100 cycles.
- Creating and removing 380 / 760 one-off attribute sets once before the loop moves the break from cycle 48 to 25 / 15 (4 cameras).

A related bug, maybe out of scope for this ticket: Replicator render products destroyed with `rp.destroy()` stay in Fabric (`rp_*`, `PostRender`, `SDGPipeline` and two pipeline nodes per render product, 5 prims per camera re-initialization), so the Fabric prim count keeps growing. Doesn't seem to be the trigger for the behavior reported above, though.

new_candidates.body:
I have a lifecycle node in which I create an image_transport object to publish camera images.
```c++
  auto req_interfaces = image_transport::RequiredInterfaces(get_node_base_interface(),
                                                            get_node_parameters_interface(),
                                                            get_node_logging_interface(),
                                                            get_node_timers_interface(),
                                                            get_node_topics_interface());
  image_transport_ = std::make_shared<image_transport::ImageTransport>(req_interfaces);
  camera_pub_ = image_transport_->advertiseCamera("image", 1);
```

This works, but the parameters are now in a weird empty namespace.
Further, they are shown twice, but they refer to the same underlying object.
ros2 param dump shows:
```yaml
ros__parameters:                                                                                                                                                                                  
    ? ''                                                                                                                                                                                            
    : ? ''                                                                                                                                                                                          
      : image:                                                                                                                                                                                      
          compressed:                                                                                                                                                                               
            format: jpeg                                                                                                                                                                            
            jpeg_compress_bayer: true                                                                                                                                                               
            jpeg_quality: 95                                                                                                                                                                        
            png_level: 3                                                                                                                                                                            
            tiff:                                                                                                                                                                                   
              res_unit: inch                                                                                                                                                                        
              xdpi: -1                                                                                                                                                                              
              ydpi: -1                                                                                                                                                                              
      image:                                                                                                                                                                                        
        compressed:                                                                                                                                                                                 
          format: jpeg                                                                                                                                                                              
          jpeg_compress_bayer: true                                                                                                                                                                 
          jpeg_quality: 95                                                                                                                                                                          
          png_level: 3                                                                                                                                                                              
          tiff:                                                                                                                                                                                     
            res_unit: inch                                                                                                                                                                          
            xdpi: -1                                                                                                                                                                                
            ydpi: -1
```

However, the parameters can still be set by passing a param dict with an empty string as the key, followed by image.compressed.<param>

This is probably connected to https://github.com/ros2/message_filters/pull/113 and was already observed in https://github.com/ros2/message_filters/issues/227
new_candidates.title: image transport parameter namespace broken for lifecycle nodes

### 🐞 Bug

RobotWrapper built from a model alone, with no collision or visual model (both default to None), then calling buildReducedRobot([...]), crashes.
The cause is that it passes list_of_geom_models=[None, None] to pin.buildReducedModel.
Expected: a reduced robot whose geometry stays None.

### Reproduction steps
```python
import pinocchio as pin
robot = pin.RobotWrapper(model=pin.buildSampleModelManipulator())
robot.buildReducedRobot([2])
```


### Relevant log output / Error message



### System Info
inocchio 4.1.0 (PyPI pin), Python 3.13, macOS 26.6 arm64.
